cells.quote: In their meta-analytic review of the GMT literature, Macnamara and Burgoyne (2023a) found a mean effect size estimate (d) of 0.05. When controlling for publication bias, the estimate dropped to 0.01 and 0.03 (i.e., no effect at all). Further, when the authors restricted their meta-analysis to published studies in which students’ measured mindsets or attitudes were significantly affected by the GMT condition compared to control comparisons, they found no statistical effect of GMT on measures of academic performance. When limiting their meta-analysis to only those few studies adhering to best-practices criteria for scientific research, they again found no effect for GMT on academic performance.
cells.note: This is a narrative review's report of Macnamara and Burgoyne's meta-analysis; the text does not state the included learners' ages, prior knowledge, settings, durations, or outcome timing.
